dashboard.title: My servers
dashboard.onboardDeployHint: Install Xrayebator on a clean VPS
dashboard.onboardImportHint: Find an installed Xrayebator and open its panel
dashboard.degradedHint: Public TLS is unavailable (Let's Encrypt could not verify the IP: port 80 is blocked by the hoster). The subscription works: keys are loaded over SSH from the server. Re-run the deploy after port 80 is unblocked to enable HTTPS.
dashboard.confirmDeleteBody: Server «{{name}}» will be removed from the app along with its keys. The installation on the server itself remains untouched.

deploy.title: Deploy server
deploy.emailProvidedHint: Recommended: renewal notices and ACME account recovery
deploy.emailWithoutHint: The certificate still works, but without Let's Encrypt notices
deploy.withoutEmailWarning: Without an email, Let's Encrypt cannot send renewal notices or recover the ACME account. You can change this later from the terminal.

active.quickstart: Setting up subscription and issuing keys...

import.title: Connect an existing server
import.hint: The app will find the installed Xrayebator and open its panel. Nothing on the server is reinstalled or updated automatically.
import.selectKeyNote: Select a private SSH key to connect with key authentication.

steps.ssh: SSH connection and host key check

sshAccess.keyNotPersisted: System keychain unavailable: the key is kept only for this app session. Select it again after restarting.
sshAccess.directRootHint: The SSH session already runs as root
sshAccess.sudoHint: A regular user with sudo access
sshAccess.sudoPasswordHint: Leave empty for passwordless sudo. Password authentication reuses the SSH password.
sshAccess.hostKeyFirstUse: The host key is pinned after the first successful login; later changes block the connection.
sshAccess.hostKeyResetTitle: Reset the pinned SSH host key?
sshAccess.hostKeyResetBody: Fingerprint {{fingerprint}} for “{{server}}” will be forgotten. Do this only after an intentional VPS reinstall; the next successful connection pins the new key.

keys.hint: Open the link in HAPP, Hiddify or any other VPN client.
keys.backendsHystNote: UDP transport: the line is already in the subscription. Clients: HAPP, Hiddify, v2rayN.
keys.backendsAwgNote: AmneziaWG 3.1 — NOT V2Ray/HAPP: import the config into the AmneziaWG/AmneziaVPN app. Full tunnel, AmneziaVPN ≥ 5.0.1.5. One key — one device: create a separate profile per device.
keys.backendsNotReady: The backend is not active yet or the config is unavailable — check the status in Server Settings.
keys.backendsNoAccess: AmneziaWG keys require saved server access (password/key in the keychain) — open Server Settings once.

settings.title: Server profiles
settings.hint: Choose how to access the server. Root + password remains the fast default; SSH keys and sudo are also supported.
settings.passwordNote: The SSH password is stored in the operating-system keychain only after a successful sign-in and is never written to app files. A distinct sudo password and key passphrase are not stored and must be entered again.
settings.createHint: One device — one key. Enter a name, protocol and copy count (profile family).
settings.protocolPrompt: Choose how traffic should bypass blocking. XHTTP — the best balance of speed and stability. For a stable connection, fast TCP is a great fit. The rest are fallback options.

protocolHint.xhttp: The most modern protocol. Low latency, excellent DPI resistance. Our default recommendation — works on both stable and unstable connections.
protocolHint.tcp: Classic TCP + Reality (Vision). Maximum speed, minimal latency. Best for stable connections: gaming, video calls, streaming.
protocolHint.tcp-utls: TCP with TLS imitation (uTLS) — resistant to active probing. Slightly slower than plain TCP, but more reliable when your ISP actively blocks.
protocolHint.tcp-xudp: TCP + QUIC-like (XUDP). Faster on unstable links, carries both TCP and UDP. Great for messengers and VoIP.
protocolHint.tcp-mux: TCP with multiplexing — several sessions in one connection. Slower on short requests, but lower overhead. For browsing.
protocolHint.grpc: gRPC — slower than others, but nearly indistinguishable from regular HTTPS traffic. Use when other protocols are blocked by your ISP.

settings.previewHint: The first profile keeps your name as-is, the rest get suffixes name-2, name-3… Each has its own subscription.
settings.empty: No profiles yet. Create the first one.
settings.deleteKeyBody: Key «{{name}}» will be removed from server «{{server}}» together with its port binding and firewall rules. This action cannot be undone.
settings.mainProfileHint: Base HAPP profile with routes. Cannot be deleted from the app — it is used by the HAPP interface and quickstart. Remove it via SSH / server menu if needed.
settings.updated: Server updated from its tracked branch!
settings.updateBranchAuto: Auto — as pinned on the server
settings.updateBranchMainHint: The proven release for everyday use
settings.updateBranchDevHint: May be unstable. Switch back to main by updating from main
settings.uninstallBody: Xray, configurations, profiles, certificates and nginx will be removed from server «{{name}}». This action cannot be undone.
settings.uninstallFailed: Failed to remove the app from the server
settings.errorNameExists: A profile named “{{name}}” already exists — delete it or pick another name
settings.fpHint: Fingerprint imitates a browser TLS signature. It is a client-side property — Xray is not restarted, other routes are not affected. Refresh the subscription in your VPN client afterwards.
settings.fpRemember: Refresh the subscription in HAPP or another client after the change.
settings.sniWarning: SNI is bound to the port, not the profile. Changing it updates ALL profiles on this port and requires a NEW link — active connections will be dropped.
settings.sniReconnectHint: Get a new link after the change and update the configuration in clients.
settings.portWarning: Changing the port drops active connections — clients need a new link. If the chosen port is already used by a compatible transport, the SNI will be changed to that port's SNI.
settings.firewallWarning: The server changed the port, but could not open the firewall rule. Open the new TCP port manually before reconnecting clients.
settings.portReconnectHint: Get a new link after the change and update the configuration in clients.
settings.serverTooOld: The server runs an older Xrayebator: expiry dates and bypass are unavailable. Update it with the «Update Xrayebator» button.
settings.revokeHint: The subscription URL is a password: whoever gets it downloads every route. Choose what to reissue.
settings.revokeTokenDesc: The old URL stops working; routes and keys stay the same. Anyone who already downloaded the config keeps connecting.
settings.revokeFullDesc: New link plus a new key (uuid) in every route. All devices disconnect and must import the subscription again.
settings.revokeFullWarning: Full revocation drops connections immediately — both for whoever got the leaked link and for your own devices.
settings.revokeFullSecondConfirm: This cannot be undone: the old key is gone for good, only a new one can be issued. Continue?
settings.revokedFull: Full revocation of «{{name}}»: new key and link
settings.expireHintBody: The date travels to the client inside the subscription and is enforced by the server: once it passes, the profile is switched off even if the client never refreshed.
settings.expireClearHint: The profile becomes unlimited; access is not interrupted.
settings.expireCleared: Expiry of «{{name}}» removed: the profile is unlimited
settings.expireFailed: Failed to save the expiry date
settings.expireEnforced: The server checks expiry every 10 minutes.
settings.expireHint: The profile will be switched off automatically on this date
settings.expireHintSoon: Expires within days — extend it, otherwise the profile is switched off automatically
settings.expireHintExpired: Expired — the server disabled this profile. Extend the date to restore access.
settings.createExpireHint: The profile is switched off automatically on the selected date. Leave it empty for unlimited.
settings.backendsHint: Extra transports on the same server. They run alongside Xray; transport access is decided by per-profile grants.
settings.backendsUnsupported: This server runs an older manager version — update it (button above) to manage backends.
settings.backendsHystNote: The key is added to the HAPP/v2rayNG subscription automatically. Clients: HAPP, Hiddify, v2rayN. One link — all devices simultaneously.
settings.backendsAwgNote: Client is the AmneziaWG/AmneziaVPN app, NOT V2Ray/HAPP. Import .conf or QR. AmneziaVPN ≥ 5.0.1.5.
settings.backendsDevNote: Hysteria 2 and AmneziaWG are in development: the interface and behavior may change from release to release.
settings.backendsCreateHint: Pick a protocol — regular VLESS or multi-protocol — and press “Create profile”. Name, count and expiry are the fields above.
settings.backendsCreateHystDesc: Fast UDP backend over QUIC: the key joins the subscription, one link — all devices
settings.backendsCreateAwgDesc: System VPN on the AmneziaWG 3.1 kernel: full device tunnel, one key — one device
settings.backendsCreateNotInstalled: Backend is not installed — install it in the “Multi-protocol backends” section below
settings.backendsCreatedPartial: Profiles created, but some keys were not issued — check the backends section
settings.backendsConfirmHyst: Remove Hysteria 2? The service, config and certificates are torn down; hysteria2 lines disappear from subscriptions; issued grants stop working.
settings.backendsConfirmAwg: Remove AmneziaWG? Interface, config and firewall rule are removed (packages and module stay in the system). All peer connections stop.
settings.backendsConfirm31On: Enable AWG 3.1 mode (HeaderProtectionKey + RandomTrailers)? Every issued client .conf must be re-downloaded. Clients need AmneziaVPN ≥ 5.0.1.5.
settings.backendsConfirm31Off: Disable AWG 3.1 mode? Configs return to the 2.0 format; every client .conf must be re-downloaded.
settings.backendsExpiryChoose: Choose the profile whose expiry you want to change:
settings.backendsConfirmRevokeHystAll: Re-issue all Hysteria 2 keys? Old passwords stop working.
settings.backendsConfirmRevokeAwgAll: Re-issue all AWG peer keys? Old .conf files stop working.
